title: Triple-Cooked Chips
summary: These chunky chips are parboiled, fried twice at different temperatures and chilled between each stage to build an exceptionally crisp shell around a fluffy centre. The extra steps take time but give a crunch that lasts well after they leave the fryer.
equipment: large heavy pot or Dutch oven (at least 5 litres) or a deep fryer
2 rimmed baking trays, one lined with kitchen paper, one with a wire rack

ingredients.item: floury potatoes (such as Maris Piper or King Edward)
neutral frying oil (sunflower, rapeseed or vegetable)

steps.title: Cut the chips
steps.text: Cut the potatoes into thick blocks, about 2x2cm and 8-9cm long, then rinse under cold water until it runs clear. Squared-off chips in this Pont-Neuf style give more flat surface to crisp up than a thinner cut.

steps.title: First cook — simmer
steps.text: Put the chips into a pan of cold water with the vinegar and 30g salt, bring to the boil and simmer for 10-12 minutes until just tender and the edges are starting to crack. Those small fissures are exactly what you want, as they turn into the craggy crust later on.

steps.title: Dry and chill
steps.text: Lift the chips carefully onto a wire rack and leave to dry for 5 minutes, then chill or freeze for 1 hour until firm. Cooling firms up the starch on the surface, which stops the chips falling apart in the next frying stage.

steps.title: Second cook — seal
steps.text: Heat the oil to 130°C and fry the chips in batches for about 5 minutes until a pale crust has formed but no real colour yet. Drain on the rack.

steps.title: Chill again
steps.text: Chill or freeze the fried chips for a further 30 minutes until firm. Drying the chips out between each stage drives off surface moisture, which is what keeps the final crust crisp rather than soggy.

steps.title: Third cook — crisp
steps.text: Heat the oil to 190°C and fry the chips in batches for 3-5 minutes until deep golden and glassy-looking on the outside. The high heat at this final stage flashes the outside into a hard, glossy shell while the inside stays fluffy.

steps.title: Season and serve
steps.text: Drain well, scatter with the flaky sea salt and serve immediately while the crust is at its crispest. Never leave hot oil unattended at any stage of frying.

tips: Dry and chill the chips properly between each stage — skipping this is the most common reason home-made triple-cooked chips turn soggy instead of crisp.
Keep an eye on the oil temperature with a thermometer; frying too hot too soon browns the outside before the inside is cooked.
Cut the chips to an even, chunky size so they all cook through at the same rate.
Fry in small batches so the oil doesn't cool down and the chips crisp rather than steam.
safety: Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: Chips are best eaten straight away, but can be parboiled and frozen after the first cook for up to 1 month. Finish from frozen with the second and third fry as above, making sure they're piping hot all the way through before serving. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
